notes:
The repository is not a device. It is the Tesseract motion-planning framework: README.md:25 calls it 'The planning framework (Tesseract)' and states 'The core packages are ROS agnostic'; README.md:84-95 lists its core packages (tesseract, tesseract_command_language, tesseract_collision, tesseract_common, tesseract_environment, tesseract_geometry, tesseract_kinematics, tesseract_scene_graph, tesseract_support and tesseract_visualization), all libraries for planning data structures, collision checking, kinematics and visualization. README.md:90 describes tesseract_environment as the manager that adds, removes, moves and modifies links and joints, and docs/page_environment.dox:4-8 calls it 'the central manager for robot state, scene graph, collision checking, and command history'; it is an in-memory planning scene, not a steppable simulator with reset, action space, reward or terminal semantics. There is no Gymnasium or MuJoCo environment to bind.

The pinned clone also contains no owned ROS node, endpoint, message, service or action. docs/page_ros_interface.dox:6-9 states that 'While Tesseract is ROS-agnostic at its core, the tesseract_ros and tesseract_ros2 packages provide ROS integration for common workflows', and docs/page_ros_interface.dox:13-21 lists tesseract_monitoring, tesseract_rosutils, tesseract_rviz, tesseract_msgs and tesseract_ros_examples, none of which is in this clone. README.md:97-101 likewise lists Tesseract ROS as a separate related repository. package.xml:14 has only the build-time ros_industrial_cmake_boilerplate helper, package.xml:76 declares build_type cmake, and the clone has no roscpp, rclcpp, rospy or rclpy dependency. CMakeLists.txt:59-70 adds only library and test subdirectories; the only executables are gtest suites and examples (collision/test/CMakeLists.txt:12-13, urdf/examples/CMakeLists.txt:1), not device-control servers. No .launch, .msg, .srv or .action file exists in the tree, and the only Python files are mine_package_info.py (package-metadata mining) and tesseract_installer.py (downloads release .deb files), neither a device interface. The card's upstream_tests value 'collision/test' is a gtest suite, not a simulator.

A RosDriver therefore cannot be written from the pinned tree without inventing endpoints, types and a device, which the rules forbid. The card has no entry_symbols, no models and no candidate classes, and no concrete device model, command set, unit range or safety limit can be sourced. The source-role preflight at work/handoff-runs/mhs-build-20261102/completion-audit/ros-next-batch-preflight-review-v1/candidate/PREFLIGHT.md:702-703 independently recommends deferral rather than manufacturing a controller; this recon agrees after reading the cited upstream files. No package code was written, no gate was run, task.json is unchanged, and no upstream code was imported or run.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Accepted the skip proposal NOT_A_DEVICE after reading the cited lines: Tesseract is a ROS-agnostic motion-planning library (README.md:25, 84-95; docs/page_ros_interface.dox:6-9 places ROS integration in the separate tesseract_ros and tesseract_ros2 repositories), the pinned tree has no .launch, .msg, .srv or .action file and no roscpp, rclcpp, rospy or rclpy dependency, and tesseract_environment is an in-memory planning scene with no step, reset or device endpoint. The author wrote no package code; the only file the review added is the check-report.json of the reviewer's gate re-run (G1, G2, G3 and G9 fail because there is no package), which the export ignores.
